subject: history
title: The 1973 Oil Shock: One Cut, One Price Jump Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says The 1973 oil crisis pushed prices up because governments printed extra money to pay for dearer oil. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - general price rises always come from governments printing extra money

The price rises started on the supply side, not the money side: the OPEC embargo cut the flow of oil, the world oil price jumped from about $3 to about $12 a barrel, and because oil and transport are inputs to almost everything, that one rise was passed on stage by stage into transport costs, factory costs and shop prices while households cut spending back.
The embargo mattered only because governments printed money at the same time
Prices rose because households suddenly decided to spend much more

questions.misconception: The 1973 oil crisis pushed prices up because governments printed extra money to pay for dearer oil.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: The 1973 oil crisis pushed prices up because governments printed extra money to pay for dearer oil. Reteach point: The price rises started on the supply side, not the money side: the OPEC embargo cut the flow of oil, the world oil price jumped from about $3 to about $12 a barrel, and because oil and transport are inputs to almost everything, that one rise was passed on stage by stage into transport costs, factory costs and shop prices while households cut spending back.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why the world oil price jumped in October 1973.
questions.answer: The OPEC embargo cut the flow of oil to importing countries, so with far less oil reaching the market the world price jumped from about $3 to about $12 a barrel.
questions.feedback: A strong answer starts on the supply side: the embargo cut the flow, and scarcity against unchanged demand quadrupled the price.

questions.prompt: What was the world oil price after the jump?
questions.feedback: Scene 2 shows the price bar at the new height: about $12 a barrel, up from about $3 before the embargo.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state the last stage of the chain and why it happens.
questions.answer: Households cut spending back, because the stage-by-stage rises in transport costs, factory costs and shop prices left them facing higher prices for fuel, transport and goods.
questions.feedback: A strong answer gives the full chain in order - embargo, price jump, transport, factories, shops - and ends with demand falling back.
